findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic — event assertions no longer validate the grant type
findings.body: The matcher `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)` does: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; return isUUID().matches(items[1]);`. The boolean is inverted: it returns FALSE when the grant shortcut matches, and returns TRUE when it does not (as long as the suffix is a UUID). Consequence: the four event assertions that now pass `expectedGrantShortcut` (AuthorizationCode "ac", Device "dg", RefreshToken "rt", Ciba "ci") will silently accept any non-matching grant as well, so tests like `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` never actually verify the grant-type portion of the encoded `Details.TOKEN_ID`. The PR author appears to have intended a positive match (`if (!... .equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`).

findings.title: Wrong substring offset when extracting grant-type shortcut from the prefix
findings.body: The encoded prefix is `sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantType(2)`, so the grant-type shortcut is at positions 4–5 (substring(4, 6)). The matcher uses `items[0].substring(3, 5)` which instead extracts the last character of the token type plus the first character of the grant type (e.g. for "onrtac" it returns "ta", not "ac"). Combined with the inverted logic above, the matcher effectively never reads the grant shortcut. Fix is `items[0].substring(4, 6)`.

findings.title: Copy-paste error in null check — rawTokenId is never validated
findings.body: Line 73 is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. It re-checks `grantType` and shows a misleading message; the actual `rawTokenId` parameter is NOT null-checked, so a null `rawTokenId` flows through to `getRawTokenId()` and into `encodeTokenId`, producing a token ID ending with just `':'`. Replace with `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

findings.title: postInit duplicate-detection only triggers on bijective collisions
findings.body: The validation `if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size())` only fires when the number of unique shortcuts differs from the number of unique grant IDs, i.e. when a collision exists in BOTH directions (or in one direction such that sizes differ). A duplicate where two factories share the same `getId()` but have distinct shortcuts, or share the same shortcut but have distinct IDs, produces the same map sizes and is silently swallowed (the second `put` overwrites the first). Because this factory is created at boot in `postInit`, such misconfigurations silently produce token IDs that cannot be round-tripped. The fix is to verify cardinalities or, better, fail fast on the first detected duplicate with an informative error.

findings.title: Javadoc claims shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters" but all implementations are 2-letter
findings.body: The new contract documents the shortcut as "usually like 3-letters", yet every actual implementation ships 2-character shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "pg", "pc", "rt", "ci", "dg", "ro", "te") and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` requires the 2-char layout. Update the javadoc to "2-character shortcut" so new grant authors do not introduce incompatible shortcuts.

findings.title: Non-default SPI method — implementations are forced to provide getShortcut() with no fallback
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` is added as a non-`default` method of the public factory interface. There is no default implementation and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` throws `IllegalStateException` if the grant's shortcut is unknown. Any third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (Keycloak extensions or downstream products) that pre-dates this SPI will now throw at token-issuance time for that grant. This is an unavoidable contract break of an SPI used by external implementations; it should at minimum be a `default` returning a deterministic unique derivation (e.g. first two chars of the grant id, padded/truncated) and a doc note pointing at this breaking change.
